answer: A lagoon of verified work can anchor trust in an agent economy: every agent must stake a refundable deposit and complete a small paid task before trading, with its record tied to that stake. A whisper of reputation follows each completed job, so honest agents accumulate cheap credibility while a sybil swarm must fund a comet-like burst of deposits for each fake identity. Attackers pay real money per identity, lose deposits on fraud, and cannot reuse one stake across many faces, making large-scale fakery far more expensive than honest participation.
